subject: Detection prob. estimation on BBS style point transects

messages.author: 046d6c28343d53da
messages.subject: Detection prob. estimation on BBS style point transects
parts:
Hello,

My question pertains to the validity of using DISTANCE sampling to estima=
te=20
detection probabilities and densities for bird data collected using BBS s=
tyle=20
road point transects and on trails in the grasslands ecozone of Canada.=20=


The purpose of this study was to determine differences in grassland bird=20=

density between roadside point transects and off-road point transects wit=
h=20
the ultimate goal of modeling species' distrbutions across the landscape=20=

(however, estimating detection probabilities is the first major hurdle).

Combined auditory and visual fixed-radius point counts were conducted alo=
ng=20
roads (secondary and dirt) and trail routes (no defined road and no ditch=
es)=20
with point count stations every 800m. Point transects on roads were=20
conducted along a 32km stretch for a total of 40 point count stations on =
a=20
route. Walking routes were paired with the road routes and generally star=
ted=20
at the sixth stop of the road route. The first stop of the walking route =
was at=20
least 800 m from the road and ran perpendicular to the road for 5 stops,=20=

paralleled the road for 2 stops, and returned towards the road for anothe=
r 4=20
stops. Bird detections were binned in the field into 100-m and 400-m band=
s=20
and each point count was 3-minutes in length (with no time intervals).

The ditches along the roads are ~20m wide (+12m wide road) and generally=20=

consist of taller non-native vegetation than the native prairie habitat t=
hrough=20
which the trail point transects were placed. Therefore, one can imagine t=
he=20
potentially large influence of the road and ditch on bird behaviour (avoi=
dance=20
or attraction) and bird species composition.=20

I understand the assumptions that are violated when roadside sampling is=20=

used; however, I am looking for a way in which to get around this problem=
. My=20
questions are as such:

1) Is it possible to estimate detection probability of birds using DISTAN=
CE for=20
data collected with only 2 distance bands (e.g., using the half-normal bi=
nomial=20
estimator)?

2) Can detection probablities for birds detected on roads be estimated by=
=20
combining all the trail and a random sample of the road point transect da=
ta=20
and (with survey type- trail or road as a covariate) then use detection=20=

probability estimates for each survey type to transform the estimates for=
the=20
respective survey types?

Thank you in advance for any comments or suggestions!

Kevin Kardynal, MSc
